messages.content: Make a video explaining how password reset works in our web app: the user says they forgot their password, the app looks up their account, emails them a one-time link, and the user opens it and chooses a new password.

I've drafted the graph and saved it. It has five parts: the user, the web app, the user database and the email service, which sits outside your app. The flow runs from the user's request, to the account lookup, to the emailed link, to the new password being saved.

I assumed the user database is part of your app's backend, and that the new password is saved to that database.

Is this graph right? If so, I'll agree the story with you next. If not, tell me what to change.
The graph looks good. I approve it.

The graph is approved. Next is the story. Here's my proposal:

- **Who it's for:** people who use the app, not its developers.
- **The one thing to remember:** a reset link works once, and only for an hour.
- **Shape:** problem, how it works, outcome. It opens on someone who can't remember their password, walks through the request, lookup, emailed link and new password, and ends with them signed in.
- **Hook:** "Someone can't remember their password."

Should I save this as the story brief and draft the script from it? You can also change any part first.
Yes, that story works for me. Go ahead and write the script.

input.request: Script for the password reset flow, following the saved brief (problem shape, for people who use the app). Hook: someone can't remember their password. Walk through: the user says they forgot their password; the web app looks up their account in the user database; the email service sends a one-time link that works once and only for an hour; the user opens the link and chooses a new password, which is saved and they are signed in. End on the user signed in.

assumptions: The app looks up the account by the email address the user gives, since the graph does not say how the account is found.
The reset link works once and expires after an hour, as the approved brief states; the graph does not show this rule itself.
The new password is saved to the same user database that held the account, as the graph's save step shows.
The user is signed in straight after saving the new password, as the brief describes.

suggestedTitleCard.title: Forgot your password?
suggestedTitleCard.description: How a one-time reset link gets you back in.

reply.text:
I've drafted the script: one scene, about 53 seconds. It opens on someone who can't remember their password, then walks through the request, the account lookup, the one-time emailed link, and the new password. It ends with the user signed in.

The draft assumes the account is found by the email address the user gives, and that the new password is saved to the same user database. It also assumes the user is signed in straight after saving it.

I suggest the title card "Forgot your password?" with the description "How a one-time reset link gets you back in."

Is the script right? If so, I'll save the title card and you can watch it at the Preview gate.
